lessons.title: Looking After My Body
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name one way to keep their body healthy and clean.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing 'This is the Way We Wash Our Hands'.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss why we wash hands/brush teeth; children sequence picture cards of a healthy morning routine.
key_questions: Why do we wash our hands?
What else keeps our body healthy?

differentiation.extension: Sequence full routine and explain each step

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of hygiene routines — evidence for PSED.2.
lessons.plenary: Class hand-washing demo recap.
lessons.home_link: Practise a healthy morning routine together.

lessons.title: Naming Body Parts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name at least 5 body parts using full words.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing 'Heads, Shoulders, Knees and Toes'.
lessons.main_activity: In pairs, children point to and name body parts on themselves and a partner, extending to less common parts (elbow, wrist, ankle).
key_questions: What is this called?
Can you find your elbow?

differentiation.extension: Name 10+ including less common ones

lessons.assessment_notes: Record vocabulary range per child — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire 'Simon Says touch your ___' game.
lessons.home_link: Play a body-part naming game at bath/bedtime.

lessons.title: Moving Different Body Parts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move specific body parts on request with control.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up wiggling fingers, then toes.
lessons.main_activity: Follow a 'body parts moving' game — stretch arms, stamp feet, twist waist — building body awareness and control.
key_questions: Which body part are we moving now?
Can you move it slowly? Quickly?

differentiation.extension: Combine two movements in sequence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note coordination and body awareness — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Freeze game combining all movements learned.
lessons.home_link: Do a 'wiggle and stretch' warm-up together.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 't'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 't' and blend s-a-t orally.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap s and a sounds with actions.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 't' sound/action; practise oral blending sat/tap using Fred Talk technique.
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend s-a-t?

differentiation.extension: Attempt writing 't' and blending independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 't' and s-a-t blending.
lessons.plenary: Sing all three sounds learned with actions.
lessons.home_link: Practise s, a, t sounds and blending sat.

lessons.title: Counting Body Parts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count sets of matching body parts (eyes, ears, fingers).
lessons.starter_activity: Count eyes, ears, noses together as a class.
lessons.main_activity: Children count fingers/toes in pairs, recording totals using dot representations.
key_questions: How many fingers do you have altogether?
How many eyes do we have as a class?

differentiation.support: Count fingers on one hand only
differentiation.extension: Count total fingers for a group of 3-4 children

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy up to 10+ — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class total count of all fingers in the room (estimate/count together).
lessons.home_link: Count fingers and toes together at home.

lessons.title: Exploring the Five Senses
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the five senses and link them to a body part.
lessons.starter_activity: Guess sounds with eyes closed (senses warm-up).
lessons.main_activity: Introduce each sense with its body part; children rotate through simple sensory stations (smelling jars, texture box, sound shakers).
key_questions: Which sense are you using now?
What body part helps you smell?

differentiation.extension: Explore all 5 and explain which body part is used for each

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of senses and matching body parts — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap naming all five senses.
lessons.home_link: Play a 'guess what I can smell/hear' game at home.

lessons.title: Printing with Hands and Feet
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use body parts purposefully to create a print pattern.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at examples of hand/footprint art.
lessons.main_activity: Children make handprint/footprint patterns using paint, creating a repeating pattern on paper.
key_questions: What pattern are you making?
What comes next in your pattern?

differentiation.extension: Create an ABAB repeating pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pattern-making and material control — evidence for EAD.1/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display prints and discuss patterns made.
lessons.home_link: Look for patterns around your home.

lessons.title: Everybody's Body is Different
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to express that all bodies are different and that this is positive.
lessons.starter_activity: Look in mirrors and notice unique features.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss that everyone looks different and that's a good thing; children say one thing they like about themselves.
key_questions: What makes you special?
Is it ok that we all look different?

differentiation.extension: Child compliments a friend's uniqueness too

lessons.assessment_notes: Note self-esteem language used — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Class round of 'I am special because...'
lessons.home_link: Tell your child something unique and wonderful about them.

lessons.title: Sound Lotto: Listening for Detail
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to distinguish between similar environmental sounds.
lessons.starter_activity: Guess a sound behind a screen (bell vs whistle).
lessons.main_activity: Play sound lotto matching recorded/live sounds to picture cards, discussing loud/quiet and same/different.
key_questions: Is this sound loud or quiet?
Which two sounds are the same?

differentiation.extension: Distinguish subtly different sounds

lessons.assessment_notes: Note auditory discrimination ability — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Class 'guess the sound' quiz.
lessons.home_link: Listen for and name different sounds on a walk.

lessons.title: Threading and Finger Strength
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to thread beads/objects to strengthen fine motor control.
lessons.starter_activity: Playdough pinching warm-up.
lessons.main_activity: Children thread beads onto laces/string, creating a pattern if able.
key_questions: Can you thread the bead onto the string?
What pattern are you making?

differentiation.support: Use large beads and shorter string
differentiation.extension: Thread small beads in a repeating pattern

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pincer grip development — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Children wear/show their threaded creation.
lessons.home_link: Practise pinching small objects (e.g. pasta, buttons) at home under supervision.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Funnybones' (Senses and Body Theme)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer a 'what happened' comprehension question.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict the story from the cover.
lessons.main_activity: Read 'Funnybones' or similar body-themed story, pausing for comprehension questions.
key_questions: What happened at the start/middle/end?
Which body part was mentioned?

differentiation.extension: Retell story events unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of sequence and detail — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Act out a funny bones dance together.
lessons.home_link: Share a story about the body/senses at home.

lessons.title: Matching Pairs (Socks, Shoes, Gloves)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find and match identical pairs.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at own shoes — 'How many do you wear? Do they match?'
lessons.main_activity: Sort a mixed pile of socks/gloves into matching pairs.
key_questions: How do you know these two match?
How many pairs did you find?

differentiation.extension: Sort subtly similar pairs and count total pairs

lessons.assessment_notes: Note matching/sorting logic — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Count total pairs found as a class.
lessons.home_link: Help sort socks into pairs at home.

lessons.title: Taste Testing Safely
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe a taste using simple descriptive words.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what tastes children already know (sweet fruit, salty crisps).
lessons.main_activity: (Check allergies first) Taste-test small safe samples (e.g. lemon, sugar, crisp) and describe using taste vocabulary.
key_questions: Was it sweet or sour?
Did you like it? Why?

differentiation.extension: Describe taste in own words unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary use — evidence for UTW.3/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Vote on favourite/least favourite taste tried.
lessons.home_link: Try describing tastes of foods at dinner tonight.

lessons.title: Self-Portrait with Detail (Senses Focus)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add sensory detail (eyes, ears, nose, mouth) to a self-portrait.
lessons.starter_activity: Look in mirror and note sensory features.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw a detailed self-portrait, adding all sensory features and appropriate colours.
key_questions: What colour are your eyes?
Where are your ears on your face?

differentiation.support: Pre-drawn face outline to add features to
differentiation.extension: Add hair detail, freckles, glasses etc.

lessons.assessment_notes: Compare detail level to Week 1 self-portrait — evidence of progress for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Compare portraits and celebrate individual differences.
lessons.home_link: Draw a family member's face together.

lessons.title: How Do Our Senses Make Us Feel?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to link a sensory experience to a feeling.
lessons.starter_activity: Smell something pleasant and describe the feeling it gives.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss how loud noises/nice smells/rough textures can make us feel different emotions; children match sensory pictures to feeling faces.
key_questions: How does a loud noise make you feel?
What smell makes you feel happy?

differentiation.support: Match one sense to one feeling with support
differentiation.extension: Explain why a sense causes that feeling

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emotional vocabulary linked to senses — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Share one sensory thing that makes each child happy.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a smell/sound that makes you feel calm or happy.

lessons.title: Following Instructions: Sensory Obstacle Trail
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to follow multi-step sensory instructions.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sequencing words first/then/next.
lessons.main_activity: Set up a sensory trail (touch a texture, then smell a jar, then ring a bell) and give instructions for children to follow in order.
key_questions: What do you do first? Then what?
Can you tell a friend the instructions?

differentiation.extension: 3-4 step instructions, repeated back first

lessons.assessment_notes: Record instruction-following capacity — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Children give instructions to each other.
lessons.home_link: Give a 2-3 step instruction involving senses at home (e.g. smell this, then tell me what it is).

lessons.title: Sensory Movement Circuit
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move through a circuit responding to different textures/surfaces underfoot.
lessons.starter_activity: Feel different textures with hands first.
lessons.main_activity: Set up a barefoot (socks) sensory path with different textured mats; children walk/balance across describing what they feel.
key_questions: How does this feel under your feet?
Was that easy or tricky to walk on?

differentiation.extension: Cross without support, describing each texture

lessons.assessment_notes: Note balance and descriptive language — evidence for PD.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Vote on favourite texture in the circuit.
lessons.home_link: Explore different textures barefoot safely at home (carpet, tile, grass).

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'p'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'p' and blend it with known sounds (pat, sat, tap).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap s, a, t sounds.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'p' sound/action; practise blending new words (pat, tap, sat) using known sounds.
key_questions: What sound is this?
Can you blend p-a-t?

differentiation.extension: Blend and attempt to write CVC words

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'p' and blending words.
lessons.plenary: Sing all four sounds learned (s,a,t,p) with actions.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending pat, sat, tap together.

lessons.title: One More, One Less
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find one more or one less than a given number up to 5.
lessons.starter_activity: Count a group of counters, add one, count again.
lessons.main_activity: Using counters/fingers, children practise 'one more than 3' and 'one less than 4' style questions.
key_questions: What is one more than 3?
What is one less than 5?

differentiation.support: Use physical counters and count aloud each time
differentiation.extension: Answer without counting from 1, using known facts

lessons.assessment_notes: Record confidence with one more/one less — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire one more/one less questions as a game.
lessons.home_link: Practise 'one more' with snacks or toys at home.

lessons.title: Exploring Sound-Making Objects
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explore and compare sounds made by different objects.
lessons.starter_activity: Guess what's inside a shaker by sound alone.
lessons.main_activity: Children explore a range of household/instrument objects, testing how to make sound (shake, tap, blow) and comparing loud/quiet.
key_questions: How did you make that sound?
Which is louder?

differentiation.extension: Compare and order objects from quietest to loudest

lessons.assessment_notes: Note exploratory investigation skills — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Create a simple class 'sound orchestra' together.
lessons.home_link: Explore sounds you can make with kitchen objects (with permission).

lessons.title: Musical Statues and Expressive Movement
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to respond to music with expressive body movement.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise freezing on the spot instantly.
lessons.main_activity: Play musical statues with varying music styles (fast/slow/creepy/happy), encouraging children to move in a way that matches the music's mood.
key_questions: How does this music make you want to move?
Why did you freeze like that?

differentiation.extension: Invent an original movement matching the mood

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe expressive response to music — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Discuss which music was everyone's favourite to move to.
lessons.home_link: Have a family dance session to different music styles.

lessons.title: Helping Each Other
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify a way to help a friend during an activity.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss a time someone helped them.
lessons.main_activity: Paired 'trust and help' activity — one child guided gently by a partner (eyes lightly covered) to find an object using verbal directions only.
key_questions: How did you help your partner?
How did it feel to be helped?

differentiation.extension: Child gives detailed multi-step directions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note cooperative helping behaviour — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Thank a partner for their help today.
lessons.home_link: Find a way to help someone at home today.

lessons.title: Describing What I Can See
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe an object using more than one descriptive word.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult describes a mystery object; children guess what it is.
lessons.main_activity: 'Feely bag' game — children describe what they feel before looking, using descriptive language (rough, round, small).
key_questions: What does it feel like?
What do you think it is?

differentiation.extension: Give 3+ descriptive words unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary range — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Reveal all objects and recap descriptions given.
lessons.home_link: Play a describing/guessing game with household objects.

lessons.title: Tweezer and Pincer Grip Activities
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use tweezers/tongs to pick up and sort small objects.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise pincer grip with fingers picking up small pompoms.
lessons.main_activity: Use child-safe tweezers/tongs to sort small objects (pompoms, buttons) by colour into containers.
key_questions: Can you pick it up with the tweezers?
What colour are you sorting?

differentiation.support: Use larger tongs and bigger objects
differentiation.extension: Use fine tweezers with small objects, sort by 2 criteria

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe pincer grip strength and control — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Count how many objects were sorted into each container.
lessons.home_link: Practise picking up small food items (e.g. peas) with fingers at mealtime.

lessons.title: Mark-Making: Labelling Body Parts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write an initial sound to label a picture.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned so far (s,a,t,p).
lessons.main_activity: Children label a simple body outline picture with initial sounds for parts they know (e.g. 'a' for arm), with adult support for spelling.
key_questions: What sound does this word start with?
Can you write that sound?

differentiation.support: Adult writes the letter, child traces
differentiation.extension: Child attempts full simple word independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record emergent writing stage — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share labelled pictures with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Practise writing initial sounds for family members' names.

lessons.title: Shape Hunt: 2D Shapes Around Us
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and find circle, square, and triangle shapes in the environment.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing a shape-naming song.
lessons.main_activity: Shape hunt around the classroom, finding and naming 2D shapes; sort found examples by shape type.
key_questions: What shape is this?
How many sides does it have?

differentiation.support: Hunt for circles and squares only
differentiation.extension: Include triangles, rectangles, and count sides/corners

lessons.assessment_notes: Record shape recognition range — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class tally of shapes found, most common shape discussion.
lessons.home_link: Spot shapes around your home and name them.

lessons.title: Looking Closely: Using Magnifying Glasses
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make an observation using a magnifying tool.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at own hand normally, then through a magnifying glass.
lessons.main_activity: Children use magnifying glasses to closely observe small objects (leaves, fabric, skin patterns) and describe what they notice differently.
key_questions: What can you see now that you couldn't before?
Does it look different up close?

differentiation.support: Adult models and asks yes/no questions
differentiation.extension: Child records observation with a simple drawing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note quality of scientific observation — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Share the most surprising thing seen up close.
lessons.home_link: Use a magnifying glass (or phone camera zoom) to look closely at something at home.

lessons.title: Texture Rubbing Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a texture rubbing using crayon and paper.
lessons.starter_activity: Feel different textured surfaces around the room.
lessons.main_activity: Children place paper over textured surfaces (leaves, bark, bricks, coins) and rub crayon over to reveal the pattern.
key_questions: What pattern appeared?
Which surface made the most interesting rubbing?

differentiation.support: Adult holds paper steady while child rubs
differentiation.extension: Combine multiple rubbings into a collage

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor control and material exploration — evidence for EAD.1/PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Compare rubbings and guess which surface made each one.
lessons.home_link: Try a texture rubbing on a surface at home (coin, leaf, wall).

lessons.title: My Amazing Body: Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to express pride in something their body can do.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about the body and senses.
lessons.main_activity: Children complete 'My body is amazing because it can ___' and share with the group, celebrating diverse abilities.
key_questions: What can your body do that makes you proud?
What have we learned about our senses this week?

differentiation.support: Adult offers example choices (run, jump, clap)
differentiation.extension: Child gives 2-3 examples with elaboration

lessons.assessment_notes: Note self-confidence and body-positive language — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Class cheer celebrating everybody's amazing bodies.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family one amazing thing your body can do.

lessons.title: Senses Quiz Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer 'which sense' questions correctly, demonstrating listening and understanding.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the five senses with actions.
lessons.main_activity: Quiz-style game: adult describes a scenario ('I use this to hear the birds') and children identify the sense/body part.
key_questions: Which sense would you use for this?
How do you know?

differentiation.support: Multiple choice with 2 options shown visually
differentiation.extension: Answer open questions without visual prompts

lessons.assessment_notes: Assess listening comprehension and recall — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Team points tally for correct answers, celebrate together.
lessons.home_link: Play a 'which sense' guessing game at home.

lessons.title: Whole-Body Obstacle Challenge (Review)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to complete a multi-skill obstacle course using balance, jumping, and crawling.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up stretches recapping the week's PD vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Combined obstacle course using all PD skills practised this week (balance beam, jumping hoops, crawling tunnel).
key_questions: Which part was the trickiest?
What skill did you use here?

differentiation.extension: Add a timed challenge or extra obstacle

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 2 PD progress across balance, coordination, and control — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down and celebrate completing the challenge.
lessons.home_link: Set up a simple obstacle course in the garden/living room.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: s, a, t, p
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall and blend all four sounds learned this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard review of s, a, t, p.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations: blending CVC words (sat, tap, pat), sound-matching lotto, sand writing practice.
key_questions: Can you blend these sounds into a word?
What sound is missing?

differentiation.extension: Blend and write 3-sound CVC words independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 2 phonics tracker for all 4 sounds and blending ability.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all sounds learned with a phonics song.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending sat, tap, pat over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Number and Shape
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, one more/less, and shape recognition in a game.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's key maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting body parts/objects, one more/one less with counters, shape hunt recap.
key_questions: How many is one more than this?
What shape is this object?

differentiation.extension: Independent completion with recording on whiteboard

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 2 maths observations for each child.
lessons.plenary: Class count-along and shape-naming recap game.
lessons.home_link: Continue shape-spotting and counting together over the weekend.

lessons.title: Senses Walk Outdoors
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use multiple senses to describe the outdoor environment.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict what senses we might use outside.
lessons.main_activity: Outdoor walk stopping at intervals to note what can be seen, heard, smelled, and felt; record with simple drawings/words.
key_questions: What can you hear right now?
Does anything smell different outside?

differentiation.support: Adult prompts one sense at a time
differentiation.extension: Record observations independently across all senses

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of sensory vocabulary in a real context — evidence for UTW.3/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Share favourite sensory discovery from the walk.
lessons.home_link: Take a 'senses walk' together outside over the weekend.

lessons.title: Senses-Themed Song Writing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to contribute an idea to a simple class song.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing a familiar tune to use as a template (e.g. 'Old MacDonald').
lessons.main_activity: As a class, create new lyrics about the senses to a familiar tune, with children suggesting words/ideas for each verse.
key_questions: What could we sing about seeing/hearing?
What rhymes with this word?

differentiation.extension: Suggest an original line independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note creative contribution and confidence — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform the finished class song together.
lessons.home_link: Sing the new senses song to family over the weekend.
